decisions.Description: Real-time crop condition intelligence platform (satellite + AI)
decisions.Action: Build or subscribe to a satellite-based crop monitoring platform (drone imagery, NDVI analysis, yield modelling) covering West Africa cocoa regions — providing 6-month advance warning of harvest shortfalls to all market participants
decisions.Best when: COCOBOD sold forward contracts based on a forecast that missed by 45% — real-time satellite crop monitoring would have flagged the production shortfall months earlier, allowing forward contract revision before the $1.3B loss was locked in

decisions.Action: Confectionery industry establishes a collective R&D fund ($500M+) to accelerate development of commercially viable cocoa-free ingredients (fermentation, cell culture, plant-derived) to commercial scale by 2030
decisions.Best when: The cocoa supply chain is structurally vulnerable at its most fundamental level — geographic concentration of an agricultural commodity in a climate-exposed region. Technology disruption (lab-grown cocoa/chocolate) is the De Beers lab-grown diamond equivalent for the confectionery industry.

cases.name: East Palestine Ohio Train Derailment (February 2023): wheel bearing failure + controlled burn releases 116,000 gallons of vinyl chloride; $2.2B in costs; 16 states contaminated; fundamental rail hazmat safety failures exposed
cases.brand_group: Railroad: Norfolk Southern Railway (NS) — total costs as of end 2024: $2.2B (cleanup + legal + settlements). Settlements: $310M (EPA/DOJ federal settlement, May 2024); $600M (class action, East Palestine residents); $22M (village of East Palestine, 2025). Rail safety enhancements: >$200M committed. Chemical manufacturers: OxyChem (vinyl chloride — informed NS tank cars were NOT at risk of explosion; this was not passed to the fire chief). First responder: East Palestine volunteer fire department (did not have access to AskRail app; 1 hour elapsed before they knew what was on the train). Regulator: NTSB (found controlled burn was likely UNNECESSARY); FRA; EPA.
cases.scale: 38 of 149 cars derailed (3 Feb 2023, 21:00 local time), East Palestine, Ohio (Ohio-Pennsylvania border). 11 cars carried hazardous chemicals (train NOT classified as hazmat train — lower safety protocols applied). 5 cars contained vinyl chloride (carcinogen). Controlled burn: 116,000 gallons vinyl chloride released. Contamination spread: 16 US states; 540,000 square miles (14% of US land area); ~110 million residents (1/3 of US population) impacted by pollution (Environmental Research Letters study, 2024). Aquatic kills: 43,000+ animals in first month. Norfolk Southern total costs end 2024: $2.2B. Root cause: overheated wheel bearing visible on camera for 20+ miles before derailment; hot box detector threshold set too high; crew not alerted in time. NTSB finding: controlled burn was likely UNNECESSARY — vinyl chloride tank cars were NOT at risk of exploding (OxyChem told NS; NS did not pass this to fire chief).

normal_flow_nodes.label: N1 — Norfolk Southern freight train (149 cars, 38 derailed)
normal_flow_nodes.description: A 149-car Norfolk Southern freight train travelling from Madison, Illinois to Conway, Pennsylvania. The train was NOT classified as a hazmat train despite 11 cars carrying hazardous chemicals — this classification would have required notification and display of cargo contents, and triggered enhanced safety protocols. 38 cars derailed at 21:00 on 3 February 2023 in East Palestine, Ohio (population ~4,700), on the Ohio-Pennsylvania border.

normal_flow_nodes.label: N2 — Overheated wheel bearing (root cause)
normal_flow_nodes.description: Root cause identified by both NTSB and FRA: a roller bearing on one of the rail cars failed due to overheating. Security camera footage from businesses along the route showed the bearing glowing red and throwing sparks for more than 20 miles before the derailment. Hot box detectors (HBDs) — trackside sensors that measure bearing temperatures as trains pass — detected elevated temperatures, but the alarm threshold was set too high to trigger an emergency stop. Norfolk Southern's procedures for communicating HBD data to train crews were inadequate and under-staffed.

normal_flow_nodes.label: N3 — Hazardous chemicals (vinyl chloride + other)
normal_flow_nodes.description: 5 cars contained vinyl chloride (a colourless carcinogenic gas used to make PVC plastic — the most widely produced plastic in the world). Additional chemicals: butyl acrylate (flammable liquid, likely ignited first per NTSB), ethylene glycol monobutyl ether, ethylhexyl acrylate, isobutylene. Total: 11 of 38 derailed cars carried hazardous materials. A tank car leaking butyl acrylate likely ignited first. 3 railcars carrying flammable/combustible material were punctured during the derailment.

normal_flow_nodes.label: N4 — East Palestine community + first responders
normal_flow_nodes.description: East Palestine volunteer fire department arrived quickly but lacked access to AskRail (mobile app identifying chemicals on derailed trains) — nearly 1 hour elapsed before first responders knew what was on the train. ~1,500-5,000 residents evacuated from 1×2-mile area. Ohio Governor DeWine and Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro ordered evacuation. Residents reported immediate health effects: respiratory irritation, burning eyes, headaches, skin rashes, nausea. Concerns about drinking water (East Palestine watershed drains to Ohio River — primary water source for many municipalities).

normal_flow_nodes.label: N5 — Controlled burn (the preventable escalation)
normal_flow_nodes.description: On 6 February 2023 (3 days post-derailment), authorities conducted a "vent and burn" — draining and igniting the vinyl chloride from 5 tank cars to prevent a feared explosion. 116,000 gallons of vinyl chloride were released and burned, producing a large black toxic mushroom cloud. CRITICAL FINDING: OxyChem (the vinyl chloride manufacturer) had informed Norfolk Southern that the tank cars were NOT at risk of exploding. This information was NOT passed to the fire chief who authorised the burn. The NTSB subsequently concluded the controlled burn was likely UNNECESSARY — making it the most damaging act of the entire incident.

normal_flow_nodes.label: N6 — 16-state contamination + $2.2B consequences
normal_flow_nodes.description: Pollution spread: 16 US states; 540,000 square miles; ~110 million residents (1/3 of US population). Aquatic kills: 43,000+ animals in first month. Leslie Run, Bull Creek and Sulphur Run visibly contaminated. Chloride and pH levels in northern Pennsylvania and US-Canada border regions were at highest levels in the prior 12 years (National Atmospheric Deposition Program study). Norfolk Southern total costs as of end 2024: $2.2B (cleanup ~$780M + EPA/DOJ settlement $310M + class action $600M + rail safety enhancements >$200M + village settlement $22M).

kpis.label: Cost
kpis.value: Normal hazmat rail transport: ~$0.03-0.05/tonne-mile (among the lowest-cost options for bulk chemical transport). Vinyl chloride: ~$800-1,200/tonne market price. No additional cost premium for HBD monitoring above minimum regulatory requirements. Insurance carried but thresholds not designed for multi-state contamination.

kpis.label: Lead Time
kpis.value: Rail is the standard mode for bulk chemical transport across the US. Typical transit: 2-5 days Chicago-Pennsylvania corridor. Vinyl chloride: produced continuously at chemical plants; shipped to PVC manufacturers in tank cars. Just-in-time delivery expected by downstream PVC plastic manufacturers.

kpis.label: CO₂ Impact
kpis.value: Rail is significantly lower CO2 per tonne-mile than truck (approximately 4× more fuel-efficient). Controlled burn of 116,000 gallons vinyl chloride: significant toxic chemical emissions. Cleanup operations: extensive heavy equipment and remediation chemical use over months.

kpis.label: Waste
kpis.value: 116,000 gallons vinyl chloride burned and released to atmosphere. Contaminated soil and sediment in East Palestine: hundreds of thousands of tonnes requiring remediation. Contaminated waterways: Leslie Run, Bull Creek, Sulphur Run required ongoing treatment. Demolished structures in most severely affected areas.

kpis.label: Customer Satisfaction
kpis.value: PVC manufacturers downstream from OxyChem lost vinyl chloride supply for the duration of the incident. East Palestine residents: severe ongoing dissatisfaction with health monitoring inadequacy, government response delays and information transparency. Public trust in Norfolk Southern and rail industry safety: critically damaged.

kpis.label: Risk
kpis.value: HIGH but structurally unaddressed: 3.1 billion tonnes of hazardous chemicals transported by rail annually in the US. Hot box detector thresholds and communication protocols were inadequate across the industry, not just NS. Train classification exemptions allowed hazmat trains to avoid hazmat protocols.

kpis.label: Quality
kpis.value: Vinyl chloride quality was not at issue — the chemical product itself performed to specification. The quality failure was entirely in the safety monitoring, classification, detection, communication and crisis decision-making systems surrounding its transport.

kpis.label: Sustainability
kpis.value: Extremely Negative: 116,000 gallons of carcinogenic gas released; 16 states contaminated; 43,000+ aquatic animals killed; ongoing soil and water remediation required. Long-term health effects on East Palestine residents (vinyl chloride is a known hepatocellular carcinogen) not yet fully determined.

kpis.label: Circular Economy
kpis.value: Low — not material to this case.

decisions.Description: Conduct controlled burn of vinyl chloride (the critical error)
decisions.Action: NS contractors advised and fire chief authorised vent-and-burn of 5 vinyl chloride tank cars to prevent feared explosion — despite OxyChem having informed NS that the cars were NOT at risk
decisions.Best when: This decision should NOT have been made — the chemical manufacturer's safety assessment (tank cars stable) was never passed to the decision-maker. The lesson: in chemical emergency decisions, the manufacturer's assessment must reach the on-site decision-maker before any irreversible action.

decisions.Action: Ohio and Pennsylvania governors order evacuation of 1×2-mile area surrounding the derailment immediately upon confirmation of vinyl chloride release
decisions.Best when: Correct and immediate — evacuation of the affected zone before the controlled burn was the right human safety decision regardless of the burn decision; should have remained in place longer than the 3 days before residents were told to return

decisions.Description: Submit full chemical manifest to EPA 7 days post-accident
decisions.Action: NS discloses full inventory of hazardous chemicals on the train (including butyl acrylate, ethylene glycol monobutyl ether, ethylhexyl acrylate, isobutylene) in remediation plan to Ohio EPA — 7 days after the derailment
decisions.Best when: This information should have been disclosed to first responders within hours — the 7-day delay before the full chemical inventory was known meant the controlled burn decision was made without complete information about all chemicals on the train

decisions.Description: Agree $310M EPA/DOJ settlement and $600M class action
decisions.Action: NS agrees to $310M federal settlement (May 2024) and $600M class action settlement for residents; commits to >$200M in rail safety enhancements including additional HBD installation
decisions.Best when: Unavoidable legal resolution; the settlement amount reflects the actual cost of the regulatory and human harm caused; NS did not admit liability or wrongdoing in either settlement

decisions.Description: Install additional hot box detectors (per EPA consent decree)
decisions.Action: NS commits to installing additional HBD devices along its network and increasing staffing to monitor and communicate HBD data to train crews in real time — the direct operational fix to the proximate cause
decisions.Best when: The single most directly responsive operational measure — addresses the proximate cause (HBD threshold too high, communication protocol inadequate) rather than the systemic causes

decisions.Description: Community health monitoring and water testing programme
decisions.Action: NS funds ongoing air quality monitoring, drinking water testing, soil contamination assessment and health monitoring for East Palestine residents
decisions.Best when: Essential for community trust restoration and for identifying any long-term health effects of vinyl chloride exposure; also required under EPA consent decree

decisions.Description: Commit to 24/7 emergency response centre with AskRail
decisions.Action: NS establishes a 24/7 hazmat emergency response centre that can be reached by any first responder immediately and provides complete chemical inventory for any NS train within minutes
decisions.Best when: Addresses the 1-hour gap before East Palestine firefighters knew what was on the train; a 24/7 response centre with real-time train manifests closes this information gap for all future incidents

decisions.Description: Lobby against Railway Safety Act 2023 (decision not taken well)
decisions.Action: Major freight railroads collectively lobbied against the Railway Safety Act of 2023, contributing to the bill stalling in the Senate. The act would have required 2-person crews and new HBD standards
decisions.Best when: This decision was taken but should not have been — blocking safety legislation after an accident that caused $2.2B in costs and contaminated 16 states was strategically and ethically wrong; the FRA subsequently confirmed the changes did not lead to meaningful safety improvement

decisions.Description: Replace CEO and announce safety transformation programme
decisions.Action: NS replaces CEO Alan Shaw (removed following activist investor campaign and NTSB criticism of interference); announces comprehensive safety culture transformation
decisions.Best when: Necessary but insufficient — leadership change signals accountability but structural safety reforms (HBD standards, hazmat classification, first responder information systems) require regulatory action beyond individual company decisions

decisions.Description: Provide $22M settlement to village of East Palestine
decisions.Action: NS settles separately with the village of East Palestine for $22M to fund community recovery, infrastructure restoration and long-term monitoring (2025)
decisions.Best when: Addresses the direct municipal costs borne by the village; part of a multi-track legal resolution across federal, class action and municipal claims

decisions.Description: Mandatory chemical manifest to first responders within 15 minutes of any derailment
decisions.Action: Federal regulation requiring railroad operators to transmit complete hazardous material manifest to all local emergency responders within 15 minutes of any derailment — via standardised digital system accessible on smartphones without app registration
decisions.Best when: The 1-hour information gap at East Palestine — where firefighters did not know what was on the train — was entirely preventable with a mandatory immediate notification system; this is the first responder equivalent of the AskRail improvement but mandatory rather than optional

decisions.Description: Lower hot box detector alarm thresholds — evidence-based national standard
decisions.Action: NTSB and FRA establish a national, evidence-based standard for HBD alarm thresholds and mandatory crew communication protocols — so that a bearing overheating for 20 miles is flagged in time to stop the train, regardless of which railroad operates the line
decisions.Best when: The bearing was on fire for 20 miles; the detector measured it; the threshold was too high; the crew was not alerted — all three failures require regulatory standards, not company discretion; NTSB recommended this; the Railway Safety Act 2023 included it but stalled

decisions.Description: Mandatory hazmat classification for any train carrying Class 3 or Class 6 chemicals above threshold volumes
decisions.Action: Revise hazmat train classification to apply to any train carrying hazardous chemicals above defined threshold volumes — regardless of percentage of total train composition; eliminates the exemption that allowed 11 hazmat cars to travel without hazmat protocols
decisions.Best when: The East Palestine train carried 11 cars of hazardous chemicals but was not classified as a hazmat train; closing this classification loophole immediately applies the relevant safety protocols — first responder notification, placarding, emergency response plans — to all trains carrying significant hazmat volumes

decisions.Description: Chemical manufacturer direct notification protocol for emergency decisions
decisions.Action: Establish a mandatory protocol requiring railroads to contact the chemical manufacturer's emergency response team and obtain their written safety assessment before conducting any controlled burn, vent or deliberate release of hazardous cargo
decisions.Best when: OxyChem told NS the vinyl chloride cars were NOT at risk of explosion; NS did not pass this to the fire chief who authorised the burn. A mandatory manufacturer-consultation protocol before any controlled release would have prevented the burn and most of the subsequent contamination

decisions.Description: Real-time wayside detector network with public data access
decisions.Action: Expand the national network of wayside detection systems (hot box, acoustic bearing, wheel impact) and make aggregate safety data publicly available — allowing researchers, regulators and communities to monitor rail safety patterns near their locations
decisions.Best when: The FRA reported that railroads added hundreds of detectors after East Palestine but the changes did not lead to meaningful improvement in the industry's safety record — suggesting the problem is threshold calibration and data communication, not detector density; public data access adds external accountability

decisions.Description: Mandatory 2-person crew requirement for trains carrying hazardous materials
decisions.Action: Require a minimum 2-person crew on all trains carrying hazardous materials — specifically to ensure one person is dedicated to monitoring wayside detector alerts, emergency communications and hazmat protocols while the other focuses on train control
decisions.Best when: The East Palestine derailment demonstrates that crew monitoring of HBD alerts was inadequate — with a 2-person crew, dedicated hazmat monitoring becomes feasible; Railway Safety Act 2023 included this requirement but stalled due to railroad and Republican opposition
